ledger.note: 27 May 1885: Wituland becomes a German protectorate. 'the remainder of the Wituland became the German Protectorate of Wituland (Deutsch-Witu) on 27 May 1885', after the Denhardt brothers' treaty with Ahmad ibn Fumo Bakari, who 'ceded, on 8 April 1885, 25 square miles of territory'. The sultan stayed on the throne.

certainty.note: The page gives an area and a location, no boundary; the 25 square miles ceded on 8 April 1885 are not located.

sources.title: Wituland
sources.note: Witu: established c. 1810, independent of nominal Pate rule by 1858, German protectorate 27 May 1885, British 18 June 1890; end 1905/1923.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has no Witu row), added because its page was opened for the Pate dossier and the Witu protectorate events (German 27 May 1885, British 18 June 1890, German renunciation 1 July 1890) are 1890s occupations the German and British dossiers need. One page: Wituland.

The sultan ceded 25 square miles on 8 April 1885 to the Denhardts (the page does not locate them) and the protectorate followed on 27 May 1885; the page says the Sultan of Zanzibar attacked Witu and that after 1890 the rulership was 'made a vassal of the Zanzibar Sultanate' (undated); it ends the protectorate in 1905 or 1923. The page does not mention the Nabahani dynasty.

Disagreement: the Pate page makes Wituland the Nabhani domain from 1858 and ends the Pate sultanate in 1895; this page has Witu founded in the 1810s as a state of its own. The end year here is the German protectorate of 1885 (sovereignty), not the page's 1905/1923.

Counterparts needing dossiers: german-empire (a Cliopatria row, 1871-1919; the protectorate of Deutsch-Witu 1885-1890), british-colonial-empire (the protectorate from 1890), pate-sultanate (this batch). Gazetteer name needed: Witu.

Reviewer af-05 (2026-10-19): the 'Witu expedition of 1890' (British troops at Witu on 26 October 1890) was removed from wars because it falls outside this dossier's life (1810-1885); it belongs to the british-colonial-empire dossier. The German counterpart is now german-africa (the slug the rest of the batch uses for the German colonies), not german-empire.
